test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 15 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Manyata rowed a certain distance downstream in 2 hours while it took her 30 minutes more to row the same distance upstream. How much time will she take to make the two-way journey in still water?
solution:
Given:

Manyata rowed a certain distance downstream in 2 hours while it took her 30 minutes more i.e. 2.5 hours to row the same distance upstream.

Concept used:

Time × Speed = Distance

While rowing upstream, the upstream speed is the difference between the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the flow.

While rowing downstream, the downstream speed is the addition of the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the flow.

30 minutes = 0.5 hour

Calculation:

Let S be the speed of the boat in the still water and R be the speed of the water.

Now,

The downstream speed = (S + R)

The upstream speed = (S - R)

According to the question,

(S + R) × 2 = (S - R) × 2.5

⇒ (S + R)/(S - R) = 2.5/2

⇒ 2S + 2R = 2.5S - 2.5R

⇒ 0.5S = 4.5R

⇒ S/R = 4.5/0.5

⇒ S/R = 9/1

Let the common ratio be Q.

The speed of the boat in still water is 9Q and the speed of the water Q.

Rowing distance = (S + R) × 2

⇒ (9Q + Q) × 2

⇒ 20Q

Time taken to complete the two-way journey in still water

⇒ (20Q × 2)/9Q

⇒ 4{4 over 9} hours

⇒ 4 hours ({4 over 9} × 60) minutes

⇒ 4 hours 26 minutes {2 over 3} seconds

⇒ 4 hours 26 minutes ({2 over 3} × 60) seconds

⇒ 4 hours 26 minutes 40 seconds

**∴ She will take 4 hours 26 minutes 40 seconds to make the two-way journey in still water.**
